This script attaches every package the analysis uses and defines every value a reader might want to change. The other scripts never call `library()` or type a number that belongs here: the intervention week, for example, is set once and used by the models, the fitted lines and both figures.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/setup.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/setup.R")
```

## Packages

[{readxl}](https://readxl.tidyverse.org/) reads the weekly surveillance workbook, [{epitools}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=epitools) computes the exact confidence intervals for each week, [{gtsummary}](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/) turns the fitted models into tables of odds ratios and rate ratios, and [{cowplot}](https://wilkelab.org/cowplot/) stacks the two panels of Figure 2. The [{tidyverse}](https://www.tidyverse.org/) provides the data handling ([{dplyr}](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/)), reading the Harris County file ([{readr}](https://readr.tidyverse.org/)) and the plots ([{ggplot2}](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/)).

The original R Markdown file also loaded [{flextable}](https://davidgohel.github.io/flextable/), which it used to convert the model tables for its Word output; the tables here stay {gtsummary} tables, so it is not needed. It loaded [{reshape2}](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=reshape2), [{svglite}](https://svglite.r-lib.org/), [{knitr}](https://yihui.org/knitr/) and [{ggthemr}](https://github.com/Mikata-Project/ggthemr) (not on CRAN) without using them, and loaded {dplyr} and {ggplot2} twice. None of these is loaded here.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| eval: false
```

## Where the data are

The data are not in this repository. The person running the analysis puts the folder that holds them in `COVID_IC_DATA_DIR`, in their `.Renviron` file, and the scripts find both files there. The original code expected the files in the working directory, with a reminder to set it (`#setwd here`).

```{r}
#| label: define-data-files
#| eval: false
```

## Study dates

These implement section 6 of the [analysis plan](analysis-plan.qmd). Week 1 begins on Friday 17 April 2020, when surveillance testing started; later weeks begin on Mondays. Face shields were required from Monday 6 July 2020, the first day of week 13, so `intervention_week` is 13. Every other part of the code that depends on the timing of the intervention takes it from here.

```{r}
#| label: define-study-dates
#| eval: false
```

## Week labels

The figures label weeks 2 to 22 by the Monday each begins. The original code typed the 21 labels out by hand in each of its ten plots; here they are computed once from the first Monday, 20 April 2020.

```{r}
#| label: define-week-labels
#| eval: false
```

## Estimation constants

Weekly intervals are 95% intervals, and hospital-acquired infection (HAI) rates are expressed per 1,000 patient-days (analysis plan, section 8.1).

## Plot constants

The red line marking the intervention falls halfway between week 12 and week 13. Point sizes, which show how many tests or patient-days each week contributed, range from 1 to 3.

Figure 2 draws daily Harris County cases on a second axis. {ggplot2} allows a second axis only as a transformation of the first, so the cases are divided by a scale factor to share the left axis, and the second axis multiplies them back. The factors are kept exactly as in the original code.
